title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: AI as necessity, National AI Strategy
sections.summary: Singapore's National AI Strategy 2.0 sees AI as a force for good, shifting from an opportunity to a necessity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Singapore believes that AI can be a potent force for good – to uplift human potential and to unlock economic opportunities, as set out in the National AI Strategy 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Notably, there is a shift in the AI strategy, seeing AI as a "necessity" and no longer just an "opportunity".

sections.label: Upstream digital security and resilience
sections.summary: The solution must go further upstream so companies and institutions build in security and resilience by design.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The solution needs to go further upstream so that companies and institutions can integrate security and resilience into their products and operations by design.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, may I ask what is the Government doing to update our regulations and what is being done to help companies and institutions implement higher digital security and resilience standards?

sections.label: Digital Connectivity Blueprint launch
sections.summary: The Digital Connectivity Blueprint was launched in June 2023 to enhance Singapore's digital infrastructure for enterprises and people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As Singapore marches on in our digitalisation journey and as we shift our AI strategy from opportunity to necessity, I am heartened that that the Digital Connectivity Blueprint was launched in June 2023 with the aim of enhancing Singapore's digital infrastructure for enterprises and people to capture emerging opportunities in the digital space.

sections.label: Tech layoffs and future-ready workforce
sections.summary: Large-scale tech layoffs occurred as firms align with new AI strategies, so the workforce must be future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One of the promises of making digital advancements was to avail better job opportunities for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But in recent times, we witnessed large-scale tech layoffs by the likes of Lazada, Google and Grab, arguably because they want to better align their organisational structure and resources with their new AI strategies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: While it is the businesses' prerogative to do so, what is clear is that our workforce must be future-ready as tech disruptions will only pick up in pace and the nature of jobs will change.

sections.label: Supporting AI-ready workforce
sections.summary: Bright minds need space and platforms to learn, research, experiment, fail, iterate, deliver and go to market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: We need to have the space and platform for these bright minds to come together to learn; to research and experiment; to fail and iterate; to deliver and go to market.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Therefore, what is the Government doing to support our workforce to be AI- and future-ready and to leverage AI to remain competitive?

sections.label: SPH Media Trust public funds
sections.summary: The first tranche of public funds was disbursed to SPH Media Trust in March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Chair, the first tranche of public funds was disbursed to SPH Media Trust in March 2023.

sections.label: SPH circulation numbers overstated
sections.summary: SPH Media Trust's Audit and Risk Committee found SPH overstated circulation numbers from September 2020 to March 2022, and a Police report was filed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In June last year, SPH Media Trust's Audit and Risk Committee found that SPH had indeed overstated its circulation numbers between September 2020 and March 2022 and a Police report was also filed.

sections.label: SPH Media Trust KPIs
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to inform the public, as SPH Media Trust's stakeholders, what KPIs SPH Media Trust must meet under the funding framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can the Minister inform the public – who are now SPH Media Trust's stakeholders; one, what are the KPIs that SPH Media Trust has to meet under the funding framework?

sections.label: SPH risk management and AI funding
sections.summary: The passage asks how SPH Media Trust addressed its risk management framework and where its subsidy appears in the Estimates, and notes over $1 billion for National AI Strategy 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Five, how has SPH Media Trust addressed its risk management framework?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I look forward to the Ministry's replies and request the officeholder to share under which line item and page of the Revenue and Expenditure Estimates the subsidy to SPH Media Trust is reflected at and what is the expenditure for 2023 and the amount budgeted for 2024/2025?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the Budget Debate earlier this week, I shared that I am glad that we commit to invest more than $1 billion over five years for our National AI Strategy 2.0 which will focus on building the infrastructure, developing our workforce and the industry.

sections.label: AI upskilling and 15,000 workers
sections.summary: The passage asks how NAIS 2.0 identifies upskilling opportunities for workers and how MCI will work with MOM to deliver 15,000 AI practitioners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Through NAIS 2.0, how do we identify opportunities for our workers to upskill and apply AI in their jobs to boost their productivity and add value to the industries that they are in?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is also anticipated that more than 15,000 workers are required in the AI field.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How will MCI work together with MOM to deliver the 15,000 AI practitioners required in the industry?

sections.label: AI governance and ethical frameworks
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MCI will introduce governance and ethical frameworks for AI, and notes Singapore launched AI Verify in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, as AI adoption grows, will MCI introduce governance and ethical frameworks to ensure AI's responsible and effective use?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Singapore launched AI Verify in 2022 as one of the world's first AI governance testing framework and toolkits.

sections.label: AI risk management crosswalk
sections.summary: The passage states that last year a crosswalk was announced with the AI risk management framework of the US National Institute of Standards and Technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: For instance, last year, it announced a crosswalk with the AI risk management framework of the US National Institute of Standards and Technology.

sections.label: MCI cybersecurity and digital consultations
sections.summary: MCI announced CISO-as-a-Service for SMEs and industry consultations for the Digital Enterprise Blueprint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Third, MCI had announced previously the CISO-as-a-Service last year, to help SMEs develop tailored cybersecurity health plans based on their risk profile and appetite.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, MCI had announced the launch of industry consultations for the Digital Enterprise Blueprint last year to bring together industry leaders, trade associations and companies across different sectors to better derive insights and solutions to meet Singapore businesses’ digital needs.

sections.label: Rise in youth sexual offending
sections.summary: SPF data shows youth offenders committing outrage of modesty and rape rose 48.6% from 109 cases in 2016 to 162 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What raises the alarm for me is this: while there is a general decrease in the overall number of youth arrests over the last decade, youth sexual offending has bucked the trend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to SPF, the number of youth offenders who committed outrage of modesty and rape offences climbed by 48.6% from 109 cases 2016 to 162 in 2020.

sections.label: Violent pornography and teen-dating violence
sections.summary: A 2019 US high school study found male adolescents exposed to violent pornography were over three times as likely to perpetuate sexual teen-dating violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: A 2019 study conducted with high school youths in US found that male adolescents exposed to violent pornography were over three times as likely to perpetuate sexual teen-dating violence.

sections.label: Body image anxiety among social media users
sections.summary: Nearly 20% of Singaporean adult social media users are at risk of body image anxiety, with men about 40% of that group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Nearly 20%, or one in five Singaporean adults who are active social media users are at risk of body image anxiety – with men representing some 40% of this at-risk group.

sections.label: Seniors engagement by SG Digital Hubs
sections.summary: The Member asks what percentage of seniors islandwide SG Digital Community Hubs engaged and the take-up of Seniors Go Digital Activity Packs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask the Ministry what percentage of seniors, islandwide, have been engaged by the SG Digital Community Hubs and what is the take-up for these Seniors Go Digital Activity Packs thus far?

sections.label: Seniors mobile plan and VintageRadio.sg
sections.summary: Eligible seniors aged 60 and above on ComCare or Public Rental get a $5.10 monthly mobile plan and $20 smartphone, and the Member asks about take-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: To qualify, individuals must be aged 60 years and above, and a current beneficiary of the Ministry of Social and Family Development's Long-Term or Short-to-Medium-Term ComCare assistance or under HDB's Public Rental Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Eligible seniors enjoy a two-year mobile plan at $5.10 per month and can purchase a smartphone for a one-off cost of as low as $20.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given the importance of online communication today, such schemes encourage more seniors to digitalise and be plugged in to the community and stay connected with the family at the same time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Ministry, how has the response and take-up rate been like among seniors for this scheme?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Members may have heard of VintageRadio.sg – a digital service designed for seniors to keep them informed, entertained and engaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Playing popular multilingual tunes from the 1950s, 1960s and 1970s and having veteran presenters such as Patrick Kwek, Brian Richmond, Rahimah Rahim and PN Bala guide them through the app are examples of how familiarity is injected into the digital-learning journey.

sections.label: Technology and personal service
sections.summary: Adopting technology need not make services less personal; technology should enhance services like fruit or herbs enhance plain water.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Adopting technology does not have to mean that services automatically become less personal or high-tech and low-touch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Instead, the use of technology must be like enhancing plain water by infusing it with fruits or herbs, adding colour, taste, nutrition even.

sections.label: National AI Strategy 2.0 funding
sections.summary: In Budget 2024, Lawrence Wong announced $1 billion for the National AI Strategy 2.0 over five years to boost Singapore's AI capability, capacity and value.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as part of Budget 2024, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced that $1 billion would be put into the National AI Strategy 2.0 over the next five years to help boost Singapore's AI capability, capacity and value with the twin goals of excellence and empowerment.

sections.label: Digitally-skilled workers needed
sections.summary: By 2025, Singapore's economy would need another 1.2 million digitally-skilled workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By 2025, Singapore's economy would need another 1.2 million digitally-skilled workers.

sections.label: Smart Nation opportunities and lives
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Smart Nation, in its 10th year, has translated to business opportunities, jobs for Singaporeans and improved lives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the Smart Nation now in its 10th year and digital being very much a part of life in Singapore, how has the Smart Nation translated to opportunities for businesses and jobs for Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: How has the Smart Nation and the push for digitalisation improved lives of Singaporeans?

sections.label: Inclusivity for seniors in digitalisation
sections.summary: The passage asks whether digitalisation has been inclusive of seniors and residents with special needs, and how Government will equip seniors with essential skills.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As a whole-of-society charges towards digitalisation, have we paused to ponder whether we have been sufficiently and adequately inclusive of our seniors and residents with special needs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Therefore, I implore MCI to spearhead the effort to ensure that in-person alternatives will always be readily available for those who are lost and feel helpless in seeking to embark on their digital journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Take our typical neighborhood library for instance: seniors would much prefer approaching the librarian or receptionist for assistance, rather than having to resort to a virtual helpdesk.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, I ask, how will the Government ensure that our seniors are equipped with the essential skills to enable them to participate meaningfully in a rapidly transforming digital society?

sections.label: MOLLY mobile library outreach
sections.summary: The passage asks MCI to update on MOLLY mobile library's outcomes since 2008 and whether outreach will expand to community clubs, senior activity centres and preschools.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since its inception in 2008, MOLLY mobile library has been travelling around Singapore bringing books, services and programmes to under-served communities which do not have ready access to public libraries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can MCI update on the outcome achieved thus far and whether there are plans to expand the scope and outreach efforts to better promote reading and lifelong learning in the community at places, such as community clubs, senior activity centres and preschools?

sections.label: AI funding support
sections.summary: They supported over $1 billion committed over five years to catalyse AI activities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Overall, they supported the more than $1 billion committed over the next five years to catalyse AI activities in Singapore.

sections.label: AI Centres of Excellence partnership
sections.summary: Minister Gan Kim Yong announced plans to partner 100 companies to set up AI Centres of Excellence and spur AI development in key sectors like manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Earlier today, Minister Gan Kim Yong announced plans to partner 100 companies to set up AI Centres of Excellence (CoEs) and spur AI development in key sectors, like manufacturing.

sections.label: Tripling AI practitioners
sections.summary: The pool of AI practitioners will be tripled to 15,000 over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will triple the pool of AI practitioners here to 15,000 over the next five years.

sections.label: AI practitioner training investment
sections.summary: Over $20 million will be invested in three years to enhance AI practitioner training for students, covering SG Digital scholarships and overseas internships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As an initial step, we will invest over $20 million in the next three years to enhance AI practitioner training for students.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This will cover AI-related SG Digital scholarships and overseas internships in AI roles.

sections.label: PAP upskilling and JTMs
sections.summary: The PAP Government has a record of investing in upskilling workers with NTUC, and 16 JTMs cover at least 1.4 million workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As Members know, the People's Action Party (PAP) Government has a consistent record of investing in upskilling and reskilling workers, often ahead of demand and in partnership with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are now 16 JTMs that identify job roles affected by various technologies, of which 13 specifically outline the impact of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These JTMs cover at least 1.4 million workers in hundreds of job roles.

sections.label: PDPC AI advisory guidelines
sections.summary: PDPC finalised Advisory Guidelines on use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems and will publish them today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Following extensive consultations with stakeholders, PDPC has finalised its Advisory Guidelines on the use of Personal Data in AI Recommendation and Decision Systems and will publish this today.

sections.label: MOLLY service usage figures
sections.summary: Since 2008, MOLLY has served over 500 institutions, received around 1.4 million visits and facilitated about 2.7 million loans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since its launch in 2008, MOLLY has served over 500 institutions, received around 1.4 million visits and facilitated about 2.7 million loans.

sections.label: Cybersecurity Act amendment plans
sections.summary: Upcoming amendments to the Cybersecurity Act will raise cybersecurity beyond Critical Information Infrastructure, with the Bill planned for introduction next week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The upcoming amendments to the Cybersecurity Act will raise the cybersecurity of foundational digital infrastructure and other systems as well as entities, beyond the Critical Information Infrastructure it covers today.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I am pleased to update Members that public consultations on the amendments were completed in January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We plan to introduce the amendment Bill in Parliament next week and will share more details then.

sections.label: Study of Digital Infrastructure Act
sections.summary: The task force is studying a new Digital Infrastructure Act to address broader security and resilience concerns beyond cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The task force is, therefore, also studying the introduction of a new Digital Infrastructure Act (DIA), to address broader security and resilience concerns of key digital infrastructure and services, beyond cybersecurity.

sections.label: Singapore quantum safe network
sections.summary: Singtel, SPTel and SpeQtral were appointed to build Singapore's first quantum safe network, expected ready by end 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singtel and SPTel, together with another local company, SpeQtral, have since been appointed to build Singapore's first quantum safe network – the first of its kind in Southeast Asia as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The network is expected to be ready by end 2024.

sections.label: CATOS harmful content detection tools
sections.summary: CATOS will develop tools and measures to detect harmful content, including deepfakes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Among other things, CATOS will develop tools and measures to detect harmful content, including deepfakes.

sections.label: SPH Media government funding
sections.summary: The Government stepped in to support SPH Media, disbursing around $320 million across FY2022 and 2023 and budgeting around $260 million for FY2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government decided to step in to give SPH Media a fighting chance in this new media landscape.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Thus far, around $320 million has been disbursed to SPH Media across financial years (FYs) 2022 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Anticipating a more challenging environment, as outlined earlier, we have budgeted to provide SPH Media with around $260 million in funding for FY2024.

sections.label: Digital reach KPIs not met
sections.summary: It kept overall reach and gained some digital subscriptions but missed KPIs on digital, youth and vernacular reach and time spent, so did not receive full committed funding.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While it has maintained its overall reach and achieved a modest increase in its digital subscriptions, it did not meet all its KPIs on digital reach, youth reach, vernacular reach and average time spent on its websites and apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Accordingly, it did not receive the full funding that was committed.

sections.label: AI workforce growth target
sections.summary: To strengthen the country's AI workforce, the aim is to increase professionals in the field to 15,000 over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In order to strengthen our country's AI workforce, we aim to increase the number of professionals in this field to 15,000 over the next five years.

sections.label: Digital economy value added
sections.summary: The Singapore Government will uphold its forward-looking governance philosophy and adopt a people-centric approach; Singapore's digital economy generated $106 billion value added in 2022, about 17% of nominal GDP, up from $58 billion or 13% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Singapore Government will uphold our forward-looking governance philosophy, and adopt a people-centric approach in implementation of the said programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Singapore's digital economy generated value added of $106 billion in 2022, or about 17% of our nominal GDP; up from $58 billion or 13% of our GDP in 2017.

sections.label: SME digital adoption rise
sections.summary: In 2023, 95% of SMEs adopted digital solutions, compared to 74% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In 2023, 95% of SMEs adopted digital solutions, compared to 74% in 2018.

sections.label: Digital Enterprise Blueprint thrusts
sections.summary: The Digital Enterprise Blueprint aims to uplift enterprises and workers in the Age of AI through three thrusts: AI-powered digital solutions, integrated digital solutions for scaling faster, and improved cyber resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The Digital Enterprise Blueprint aims to "Uplift our enterprises and workers in the Age of AI".

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will do this through three thrusts: first, we will empower enterprises to be smarter through using AI-powered digital solutions; second, we will support our enterprises to scale faster through adoption of integrated digital solutions; third, we will equip enterprises to be safer by improving their cyber resilience.

sections.label: SMEs using AI solutions
sections.summary: In 2023, over 3,000 SMEs adopted and benefited from these AI-enabled pre-approved solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In 2023, over 3,000 SMEs have adopted and benefited from these AI-enabled pre-approved solutions.

sections.label: Generative AI for Digital Leaders
sections.summary: IMDA is launching Generative AI for Digital Leaders, where tech partners work with enterprises to develop and implement GenAI solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: IMDA is launching a new initiative called Generative AI for Digital Leaders, where tech partners, including tech giants, will work with participating enterprises to help them develop and implement innovative GenAI solutions.

sections.label: Integrated digital solutions for SMEs
sections.summary: Stove-piped solutions limit digital potential, so efforts will include more integrated solutions, interoperability requirements and cloud-native solutions under SMEs Go Digital.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Such stove-piped solutions also prevent enterprises from harnessing the full potential of digital, including deriving business insights from data analytics.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: So, we will step up our effort to: (a) include more integrated digital solutions under the SMEs Go Digital programme; (b) stipulate interoperability requirements where possible for these solutions; and (c) encourage more of these solutions to be cloud-native for greater scalability.

sections.label: Cybersecurity incidents among enterprises
sections.summary: A survey found over eight in 10 Singapore enterprises encountered at least one cybersecurity incident in a year, with almost all suffering negative business impact.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The same survey found that over eight in 10 enterprises in Singapore encountered at least one cybersecurity incident in a year and almost all of them suffered negative business impact.

sections.label: Co-funding support for eligible enterprises
sections.summary: Eligible enterprises can receive co-funding support to defray the service cost, and 55 SMEs have benefited so far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Enterprises that are eligible can receive co-funding support to defray the cost for this service.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Thus far, 55 SMEs have benefited from this scheme.

sections.label: Rising share of technology jobs
sections.summary: Demand for technology talent remains strong, with technology jobs rising from 4.5% of total employment in 2018 to 5.2% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Currently, the demand for technology talent remains strong with technology jobs across the economy account for a rising share of total employment: from 4.5% in 2018 to 5.2% in 2023.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator talent pipeline
sections.summary: Minister Josephine spoke about developing AI talent and enhancing TeSA, which has placed over 17,000 locals into tech jobs and upskilled over 231,000 professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Minister Josephine spoke earlier about our efforts to develop a pipeline of AI talent and AI-equipped workforce, including efforts to enhance the existing TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) initiative which, to date, has placed more than 17,000 locals into tech jobs and upskilled and reskilled more than 231,000 professionals.

sections.label: Companies pledging skills-based hiring
sections.summary: The number of companies pledging support for skills-based hiring doubled from 100 to 200 within three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Within three months, I am glad to share that the number of companies pledging their support for skills-based hiring has doubled from 100 to 200.

sections.label: Accenture skills-based hiring results
sections.summary: Accenture adopted skills-based hiring with a multi-stage assessment, reducing time to hire by 75% and increasing quality talent pipelines by 40%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Accenture is another company that has adopted skills-based hiring.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: They adopted a rigorous multi-stage assessment, focusing on skills, competencies and growth potential which proved to reduce time to hire by 75% and increased quality talent pipelines by 40%.

sections.label: Government AI help for businesses
sections.summary: The Government will help businesses, especially SMEs, harness AI, with IMDA launching 22 Industry Digital Plans and incorporating AI into digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Government will assist businesses, especially the SMEs and their employees, to harness AI for their benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: So far, IMDA has collaborated across various sectors to launch 22 Industry Digital Plans (IDPs).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In the upcoming updates of these IDPs, the authority will also incorporate sections on AI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Furthermore, under the SME Go Digital Programme, the IMDA will collaborate with the tech industry to incorporate AI technologies into the pre-approved digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Presently, 20% of digital solutions are driven by AI, benefitting over 3,000 SMEs.

sections.label: Households claiming digital vouchers
sections.summary: Households have claimed over $1 billion in digital vouchers since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Households have claimed over $1 billion in digital vouchers since 2020.

sections.label: Build For Good problem statements
sections.summary: Ahead of Build For Good 2023, organisers collected over 700 problem statements from the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Ahead of Build For Good 2023, the organisers collected over 700 problem statements from the public.

sections.label: MoneySound development paused
sections.summary: After considering concerns about installation, maintenance and how it worked, the team paused MoneySound development three months after it began.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: They had some concerns about the installation, the maintenance of the device and also about how it worked.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, after considering these insights, the team has paused the development on MoneySound three months after it began.

sections.label: Citizen and business satisfaction
sections.summary: Between 2014 and 2023, citizen satisfaction with Government services rose from 73% to 83% and business satisfaction from 69% to 83%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Between 2014 and 2023, citizen satisfaction with Government services has improved from 73% to 83%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Over the same period, business satisfaction with Government services has also risen, from 69% to 83%.

sections.label: ScamShield downloads
sections.summary: ScamShield, a product addressing a difficult day-to-day problem, appears well-received with 850,000 downloads.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It is a difficult problem that affects us on a day-to-day basis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And now, we have a product, ScamShield, and it appears to be well-received – 850,000 downloads.

sections.label: Seniors smartphone ownership and assistance
sections.summary: 89% of seniors aged 60 and above owned a smartphone in 2022, up from 74% in 2017, and over 16,000 assistance packages were approved since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Chairman, 89% of seniors aged 60 years and above own a smartphone in 2022 and this has increased from 74% in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And our Mobile Access for Seniors' scheme has approved more than 16,000 assistance packages for low-income seniors since the launch of the scheme in 2020.

sections.label: AI compute investment
sections.summary: Up to $500 million will be invested to ensure Singapore has sufficient high-performance compute for AI innovation and capacity building.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To that end, we will be investing up to $500 million to ensure that Singapore can have sufficient high-performance compute to support our ambitions in AI innovation and capacity building.

sections.label: 10G NBN upgrade investment
sections.summary: IMDA will invest up to $100 million to help operators upgrade infrastructure and services, targeting completion of the 10G NBN upgrade by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: IMDA will be investing up to $100 million to support operators in upgrading their infrastructure and offering innovative services at competitive prices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This is to cater for upcoming opportunities in areas, such as AI, immersive digital experiences and autonomous solutions, which will require higher bandwidth connectivity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We target to complete the upgrade to the 10G NBN by 2026 and expect more than half a million households to sign up for and benefit from higher-speed broadband in the next five years.

sections.label: Cybersecurity R&D programme office
sections.summary: A CyberSG R&D Programme Office was established at Nanyang Technological University with $62 million allocated to support cybersecurity research.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: For cybersecurity, we have established a CyberSG research and development (R&D) Programme Office at the Nanyang Technological University, with allocated funding of $62 million to support cybersecurity research.

sections.label: Digital infrastructure and R&D investment
sections.summary: Singapore invests in digital infrastructure and R&D to advance digitalisation goals, an approach that has succeeded in its Smart Nation journey.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: At the same time, we have to look ahead to the horizon and invest in digital infrastructure, research and development so that we can facilitate ahead of time our goals for digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information and Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So far, this approach has been successful, and there is much more that this approach can deliver for Singapore as we enter the second decade of our Smart Nation journey.

sections.label: Separate line item for SPH Media Trust
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister to consider a separate line item for SPH Media Trust given the large grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In view of the large grant, can I invite the Minister to consider, perhaps in the future, a separate line item for SPH Media Trust?

sections.label: KPIs for SPH Media funding
sections.summary: A Member suggests including SPH Media KPIs, such as reach, engagement and vernacular targets, in the Budget Book's KPI section.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The second point pertains to some of the KPIs that the Minister shared, certain KPIs that were mapped were not met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: At the end of every Ministry in the Budget Book, there is a section on KPIs with key indicators of how the Ministry looks upon what services are rendered to the public and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: It would be helpful also perhaps, in view of the longer-term funding of SPH Media, I would suggest, to include some of those KPIs in that KPI section in the Budget Book, so that the public also can be informed of where it is doing well and where it is not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: For example, I think the Minister spoke about reach, engagement, vernacular targets.

sections.label: Trusted brands in Singapore
sections.summary: In the 2023 report, all top five and eight of the top ten most trusted brands in Singapore are homegrown public service media entities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you look at the 2023 report, you will find that within Singapore, amongst the top five most trusted brands, all are public service media entities from Singapore, homegrown.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If you look at the top 10, then eight of them are our own public service media entities.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If we were to remove our own public service media entities, what we are really left with will be CNN, which is a US company.

sections.label: Inadequacy of current indicators
sections.summary: The speaker says applying a metric is not easy and the current set of indicators is probably very inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is not so easy to apply a metric.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are very cognisant of the fact that the set of indicators that we use today is probably going to be very inadequate.
